I’ve been testing out Windows 10 on a Lumia 640 for the past four days and am generally pleased with the performance. I posted my thoughts on Reddit as well (I kind of have one foot here and one foot there :))

Configuration Lumia 640 (AT&T) unlocked with 64GB micro SDXC card. Using it on Telus in Canada.

Performance

Very responsive, I am very impressed with the speed of the OS with this configuration. Especially when it comes to switching between apps.

Communication

It has no problems connecting to the Telus network on LTE. Voice quality seems to be the same as before the upgrade. I can get 60Mbs down and 8Mbs up on LTE.

Groove Music

I was surprised to find out that Groove supports lossless AAC now (I haven’t heard MS or anyone talk about it) which is fantastic for people with Apple devices that don’t want to convert their lossless collection. This is in addition to the advertised support for FLAC. I can report both work flawlessly and the ID3 tags are read accurately. While the app is usable it’s still lacking a lot of options (EQ, Start-up options, lock screen controls and album art, etc). One annoying thing I did encounter is that somehow my Zune desktop playlist and library ended up in the MS cloud and Groove populated its playlist and library with that data. Of course none of that exists on the devise so I had a nice playlists of music that was unavailable which was very annoying. I cleared this data using the Groove Music on my desktop. I recommend doing that first before doing the Windows 10 upgrade.

Edge browser

Fast and responsive. Good browser especially now that the address bar is back on the bottom of the screen.

People

Not sure how I feel about the polka dots on the live tile but the app itself works fine. The only annoying thing is that it doesn’t seem to consolidate contacts (the obvious ones) from different sources (Gmail, outlook, facebook). Also its missing Linked In integration.

Notifications

This is a much better implementation than Win 8.1. I love the inline reply to texts. Settings The most despised thing in Win 8.1 was the setting screen. It was a convoluted mess. Win 10 cleans it up nicely in logical categories. There is also a search feature as well.

Outlook Mail

A much better client than the Win 8.1 version. It just needs a consolidated mail box. I hate switching accounts.

Calendar

A much much better implementation of the calendar app. I hated the Win 8.1 version but I love this one. Clean and beautiful.

File Browser

Finally a built in file browser. It’s very basic but it’s a start.

Storage options

Storage sense will now let you set where new items such as apps, music, etc are saved to. You can choose phone or SD card. Also it will let you move your apps on your phone to the SD card (assuming the author of the app hasn’t blocked this feature, I’ve only run into a few that have). An sd card is a must for a 8GB device and I’m glad there is a decent implementation of this on Win 10.

Notes

After the upgrade I had all kinds of stability issues with apps crashing left and right. I did a “reset your phone” (including the option to erase the sd card). Once I did that the system was pretty stable. Also do an update all from the Store (There are a lot of updates).

It's articles like this that make me want to upgrade my 640 as well, but I just can't risk losing my daily driver. I have Win10 on all my laptops, tablets, netbooks, etc, and will be tossing it on the Xbox as soon as I can, but I have to force myself to wait on the phone. Great review, by the way!

Thanks! It is a beta and it does have issues, it all depends on your tolerance level. Today on my way to work Groove randomly crashed. I'm not sure if it hit a track it didn't like or it was random. I think it's one more beta release away from being OK as a daily driver for most people.
